trails.title: The 250 Trail: Austin — East Side Standards
trails.hook: Walk the East 11th and 12th spine where Black and Mexican-American Austin built the warmth the whole city later called 'weird' — from a 1945 Chitlin' Circuit juke joint to the brisket and masa masters who planted on the same blocks.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Chicago — The Neighborhood Mosaic
trails.hook: One city, 77 official pieces, each built by somebody who just got here. Eat the mosaic — Polish sausage to carnitas, dim sum to glögg — on the streets where the blues plugged in.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Denver
trails.hook: Welton Street was the Harlem of the West. Follow the music from Five Points' jazz corridor into RiNo's mural economy — one century, one improvised neighborhood.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Houston — The City That Eats in Every Language
trails.hook: The most diverse big city in America wrote its menu in every language it speaks. Drive the corridors where immigration did the cooking — from the Navigation Boulevard taqueria that taught America to crave tacos al carbon to Viet-Cajun crawfish on Bellaire.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Kansas City
trails.hook: Follow the smoke from the jazz clubs of 18th & Vine to the pits that same neighborhood built — one long, low-and-slow lineage of Black Kansas City genius.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Los Angeles
trails.hook: Follow the tortilla from the birthplace of Los Angeles across the river to Boyle Heights and up old Route 66 — the east side where mariachis, murals, and family kitchens keep the city's real memory.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Miami — Two Exile Capitals
trails.hook: Two capitals-in-exile, a few miles apart — cafecito windows and domino tables on Calle Ocho, griot and kompa up Northeast Second. Walk the axis where two islands rebuilt their homelands and remade an American city.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Nashville
trails.hook: Before Music Row had a sound, Jefferson Street had the song. Follow the R&B corridor and the writers' rooms as one long verse.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: New Orleans
trails.hook: Three hundred years of French, Spanish, African, Caribbean, and Acadian hands in the same pot. Walk from Congo Square's drum circles to the po-boy counters and the families still stirring the roux.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: New York City — Main Streets of Arrival
trails.hook: A mile and a half, five languages, 160 years of arrival. From a preserved tenement on Orchard Street to hand-ripped noodles born in a Flushing basement stall — eat the main streets where New York keeps becoming America.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Phoenix
trails.hook: The street that answered a law with a paintbrush — then fed a whole food revolution. Walk Calle 16 and eat the Mexican-American Phoenix that painted its own name on the wall.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Portland — Pods & Portals
trails.hook: From the hand-built gates of Old Town Chinatown to the griddles immigrants turned into an institution: Portland's story told through its doorways and its food carts.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Salt Lake City
trails.hook: From a pioneer's-eye overlook to State Street's global kitchens — the Crossroads of the West doing what it's always done: taking in the world and feeding it well.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: San Francisco — Dragon Gate to the Mission
trails.hook: From dim sum under pagoda roofs raised in defiance to a midnight super burrito wrapped in foil — walk three miles and 250 years through the two San Francisco neighborhoods that survived everything by feeding everyone.

trails.title: The 250 Trail: Smoky Mountains — Handmade in the Hollers
trails.hook: An eight-mile loop of carvers and broom-tiers, a gristmill grinding since 1830, and bluegrass from a rocking-chair porch — this is the Smokies that made things, and made music, long before it made vacations.
